subsystems.name: Exoplanet surveys
subsystems.role: measure how common planets of each size and orbit actually are.

subsystems.name: Stellar and galactic context catalogue
subsystems.role: places each planet system in its wider setting.
parts: stellar spectroscopy for composition and age

subsystems.name: Orbital and tidal modelling
subsystems.role: tests whether a stabilising moon or a benign giant-planet arrangement can survive for billions of years.

subsystems.name: Interior and geodynamic modelling
subsystems.role: tests whether plate tectonics and a magnetic dynamo are likely outcomes for a given planet.

subsystems.name: Climate and habitability modelling
subsystems.role: tests whether surface liquid water can persist.

subsystems.name: Statistical inference framework
subsystems.role: converts all of the above into frequency estimates and tests whether the proposed prerequisites are truly independent.

buildSteps.title: State the hypothesis as measurable quantities
buildSteps.detail: Turn each claimed prerequisite — a large stabilising moon, plate tectonics, a magnetic dynamo, a Jupiter-class shield, a quiet galactic neighbourhood — into something with a number attached, so it can be counted or modelled.

buildSteps.title: Measure the baseline planet population
buildSteps.detail: Transit and radial-velocity surveys give the occurrence rate of rocky planets in temperate orbits around different star types, after correcting for what each survey could and could not have detected.

buildSteps.title: Measure the secondary conditions
buildSteps.detail: Attempt to observe the prerequisites themselves: moons around exoplanets, planetary axial tilt, auroral radio emission as a dynamo signal, atmospheric composition as a tectonics clue. Most of these are at or beyond today's detection limits.

buildSteps.title: Test whether the prerequisites are independent
buildSteps.detail: Several proposed requirements may be consequences of the same event — a giant impact can produce a large moon and set the planet's spin — so the models check for shared causes before the requirements are multiplied together.

buildSteps.title: Build the joint probability model
buildSteps.detail: Combine the measured rates and the modelled dependencies into one probability that a planet has all the required conditions at once, rather than treating each as a separate lucky draw.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against the one known case
buildSteps.detail: Earth is the only planet known to host complex life, so the model is checked against Earth's own history — its moon, tectonics, dynamo and impact record — and against null models that assume no special requirements at all.

buildSteps.title: Refine with better instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each new survey or spectrograph narrows the uncertainty on one term in the model, so the exercise is repeated rather than run once.

buildSteps.title: Report as constraints, not verdicts
buildSteps.detail: The output is a range for how common complex-life-capable planets may be, plus which prerequisites are doing the limiting — not a yes-or-no answer.

prerequisites.why: without measured occurrence rates for planets, sizes and orbits, the whole calculation has no baseline.
planet statistics only make sense when corrected for the star types, ages and environments actually surveyed.
plate tectonics, dynamos and long-term habitability cannot be measured directly, only modelled.
the stabilising-moon argument cannot yet be tested, because almost no exomoons or planetary tilts have been measured.

prerequisites.tech: Atmospheric characterisation of temperate rocky planets
prerequisites.why: it is the main indirect window onto tectonics and surface conditions on other worlds.
observing biases would otherwise masquerade as evidence that certain conditions are rare.

pathway.milestone: well-measured occurrence rates for planets of different sizes and orbits
pathway.unlocks: a quantitative baseline for how common the starting conditions are.

pathway.milestone: atmosphere measurements for a handful of temperate rocky planets
pathway.unlocks: first real evidence on whether such worlds are habitable or stripped bare.

pathway.milestone: reliable detections of exomoons and planetary axial tilts
pathway.unlocks: direct tests of the stability arguments that currently rest on theory alone.

pathway.milestone: a survey of Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars
pathway.unlocks: a statistical answer to whether complex life needs a rare combination of conditions or is common.
